prior_findings.evidence: scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:538-552 accepts only fresh descendants satisfying Test-IsClaudeProc; the former arbitrary-subtree tier is gone. Get-WtCommandLine also adds -NoProfile at line 746.

scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:336-376 validates the header and bounded tail, while -DeepValidate enables a whole-file scan. Default operation still intentionally cannot detect corruption between the header and final 64 KB.

scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:420-463 requires a terminated record carrying the expected sessionId and beginning at or after LatestLength; timestamp-only and sessionId-less changes cannot prove resumption.

scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:514-531 recognizes the resolved image/path, a surviving command shim, and standard Claude Code CLI module paths. The arbitrary-descendant fallback that made K1 only partial is gone.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:538-552 removes generic subtree attribution, and line 746 launches the tab shell with -NoProfile. An unrelated descendant no longer qualifies merely by ancestry.

scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:299-311 and 424-446 reconstruct ordinary records straddling launch and require proof to begin at or after LatestLength. However, Get-LastRecordBoundary returns the arbitrary tail-window start when no LF exists inside the window, so records longer than 64 KB are still split.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:447-463 ignores sessionId-less records and returns RESUMED only for a complete post-snapshot record carrying LatestSessionId.

scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:270-292 and 426-428 still turn unstable, truncated, replaced, or repeatedly short reads into retryable null evidence and ultimately UNCONFIRMED. This remains a conservative refinement, not a false pass.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:997-1012 opens RunLockHandle without an explicit finally/disposal path; cleanup remains dependent on process termination and is not release-blocking.

findings.title: Tail-limited boundary search can begin inside a long record
findings.detail: If the last complete record boundary lies more than TailBytes behind EOF, Get-LastRecordBoundary finds no LF and returns $start, although $start is not known to be a record boundary. A record longer than 64 KB that straddles launch is therefore decoded from its middle. Its foreign sessionId can be missed, after which a later expected-session record can yield RESUMED and VERIFIED. Empty files and no-newline files of at most 64 KB correctly return zero; the failure is specifically the no-newline-in-window case with a nonzero start.
findings.recommendation: Search backward in additional chunks until LF or BOF is found, or persist enough prefix state to reconstruct the record. Never label the tail-window start a complete-record boundary without observing LF immediately before it.

findings.title: Broad CLI module-path content match is forgeable
findings.detail: The second entry-point rule accepts any descendant whose command line contains an @anthropic-ai/claude-code directory, not necessarily the CLI entry point. Expected arguments are also checked as substrings, so values such as --continue-helper qualify. A shim or helper can therefore start an unrelated long-lived process with a matching path fragment and argument text; under -Fresh that process is sufficient for STARTED and VERIFIED. The harness tests only a genuine-looking cli.js command and ping without forged text.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the shim to the exact durable runtime executable and canonical CLI script, parse the candidate command line into argv, and compare the entry-script path and argument tokens exactly. Remove the package-directory-only fallback.

findings.title: Expected-sessionId requirement can starve legitimate resumes
findings.detail: The supplied measurement establishes prevalence across stored records, not that Claude emits a matching-sessionId record during the 45-second unattended verification interval. It also reports one of 29 transcripts with no qualifying non-header record, which this algorithm can never prove. A healthy resumed CLI that appends only sessionId-less records, or emits no record until user interaction, remains UNCONFIRMED and fails normally.
findings.recommendation: Measure actual --continue startup behavior across supported installation versions and hosts. Use a launch-time session-specific signal that Claude reliably emits, or document and explicitly accept UNCONFIRMED operation if no reliable signal exists; transcript-wide prevalence is not a latency/reliability guarantee.

findings.title: Argument verification uses substring rather than argv identity
findings.detail: Contains() accepts expected argument text embedded in another token, including --continue-extra and unrelated values containing 1000000. This contributes to the forgeability in H2 and does not prove the requested invocation exactly.
findings.recommendation: Parse the Windows command line with CommandLineToArgvW-compatible semantics and compare complete argument tokens and required value adjacency.

harness_reason: The 134 clean assertions and twelve defect-specific mutants are meaningful evidence, and the new J1-J3 tests genuinely exercise their named regressions. Remaining untested cases include a last record exceeding the 64 KB boundary-search window, a forged @anthropic-ai/claude-code helper command line, substring lookalike arguments, real supported Claude installations beyond the synthetic CLI process, whether --continue emits a qualifying sessionId promptly without interaction, the reported transcript containing no non-header sessionId, concurrent replacement/truncation throughout polling, lock-creation failure and explicit disposal, and a complete end-to-end scheduled-task/wt/PATH/launch/poll/output/exit run.
verdict_reason: The bounded record-boundary algorithm can hide a foreign sessionId and permit a later false RESUMED result, while the broad CLI content rule can attribute a forged non-Claude descendant. Separately, the new sessionId requirement is not shown to succeed during normal unattended startup and demonstrably cannot prove at least one measured transcript class, creating a normal-operation false-negative risk.
